name: klin
description: NestJS or plain Express/Fastify + Better Auth + Prisma + Vite (TanStack Router) or Next.js + TanStack Query/Form + shadcn/ui, in a Turborepo with shared Zod validators.

steps.title: Stack
steps.heading: Pick your engine.
steps.subtitle: How the API is built and served, where the data lives, and what runs the web app.

steps.title: Auth
steps.heading: Decide who gets in.
steps.subtitle: Better Auth runs sessions, cookies and the tricky flows for you.

steps.title: Toolbox
steps.heading: Fill the toolbox.

questions.title: Framework
questions.message: How should the API be built?

questions.title: Web app
questions.message: What should run the web app?

nest.label: NestJS
nest.about: Modules, controllers and dependency injection, with nestjs-zod turning the shared Zod schemas into DTOs. Pick it when the API will grow and a team wants structure.

plain.label: Plain
plain.about: No framework on top: an app file, route modules and plain service functions. Less ceremony, with the same shared Zod schemas, auth guards and response envelope.

express.label: Express
express.about: The classic Node.js server with the biggest middleware ecosystem. NestJS runs on @nestjs/platform-express; plain mode uses Express 5 with async error handling.

fastify.label: Fastify
fastify.about: A faster server with schema-first routes and built-in pino logging. NestJS runs on @nestjs/platform-fastify; plain mode types every route straight from your Zod schemas.

password.label: Email & password
password.about: Classic email and password with sign-up, verification and password reset. Better Auth hashes passwords and stores sessions in your database; the forms live in apps/web/src/features/auth.

google.label: Google
google.note: Add GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET to .env to switch on Google sign-in
google.about: Sign in with Google over OAuth: the button, callback and account linking are wired. Add GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET to .env to switch it on.

github.label: GitHub
github.note: Add GITHUB_CLIENT_ID / GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET to .env to switch on GitHub sign-in
github.about: Sign in with GitHub over OAuth: the button, callback and account linking are wired. Add GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET to .env to switch it on.

magic-link.label: Magic link
magic-link.about: Passwordless sign-in: people type their email and click the link they get. Until email is set up, links are printed to the API logs so you can click them locally.

two-factor.label: Two-factor (TOTP)
two-factor.about: Authenticator-app codes with backup codes, switched on from the security settings page. It builds on email & password, so that gets snapped on too.

passkey.label: Passkeys
passkey.hint: Face ID, Touch ID, security keys
passkey.about: Face ID, Touch ID and hardware keys over WebAuthn. People add passkeys in their security settings and can then sign in without a password.

organizations.label: Organizations & RBAC
organizations.about: Teams with invitations, roles and permissions, plus an organization switcher in the sidebar. Access rules live in packages/auth/src/permissions.ts and guard API routes and UI alike.

admin.label: Admin dashboard
admin.about: An admin area to list, ban and impersonate users, with sign-up stats. Only users with the admin role get in, and the seed script makes the demo user one.

api-keys.label: API keys
api-keys.hint: let users call your API from scripts
api-keys.about: People create API keys in settings to call your API from scripts and CI. Keys are stored hashed, can expire, and work anywhere a session cookie does.

postgres.label: PostgreSQL
postgres.about: PostgreSQL through Prisma's pg driver adapter. Docker Compose starts a local server (pnpm db:up) and DATABASE_URL in .env already points at it.

mysql.label: MySQL
mysql.about: MySQL or MariaDB through Prisma's MariaDB adapter. Docker Compose runs a local server, or point DATABASE_URL in .env at your own.

sqlite.label: SQLite
sqlite.hint: zero setup, a file on disk
sqlite.about: One file at packages/db/data/dev.db, with nothing to install or start. Great for prototypes; switch later with klin add postgres.

vite.label: Vite
vite.about: A single-page React app with TanStack Router's typed file routes and beforeLoad guards. Vite forwards /api to the API in dev, and nginx does in production.

next.label: Next.js
next.about: The App Router: pages render on the server, signed-out visitors are redirected before anything loads, and /api is rewritten to your API. TanStack Query and Form work just like with Vite.

cors.label: CORS
cors.hint: only your web app may call the API
cors.about: Browsers may only call the API from your web app's origin (WEB_URL), with cookies allowed. In development the Vite proxy keeps requests same-origin anyway.
cors.warnOff: Without it the API sends no CORS headers, so browsers block calls from any other origin. Fine only if the web app and the API share one domain in production.

helmet.label: Helmet
helmet.about: Secure HTTP headers on every API response: no MIME sniffing, no framing, a strict referrer policy and more. Uses helmet on Express and @fastify/helmet on Fastify.
helmet.warnOff: API responses go out without security headers, so browsers may sniff content types and other sites can frame your pages. Set the headers at your proxy if you skip it.

rate-limit.label: Rate limiting
rate-limit.about: Caps each IP at 120 requests a minute so one client can't flood the API; health checks are exempt. Uses @nestjs/throttler, express-rate-limit or @fastify/rate-limit, tuned in one place.
rate-limit.warnOff: Nothing stops one client from flooding the API or hammering sign-in with password guesses. Put a limit at your proxy or CDN if you skip it.

email.label: Transactional email
email.about: Resend with React Email templates in packages/email: verification, reset, magic-link and invite emails are wired. Preview the templates with pnpm email:dev.

uploads.label: File uploads
uploads.about: Direct-to-storage uploads with presigned URLs for S3, R2 or any S3-compatible store. Docker Compose runs RustFS (S3-compatible) locally, and the avatar upload shows the whole flow.

queues.label: Background jobs
queues.about: BullMQ jobs on Redis, with a welcome email queued on every sign-up. Docker Compose starts Redis, and workers run inside the API process to begin with.

i18n.label: Internationalization
i18n.about: i18next set up with English, and every UI string already goes through t(). Add a language by dropping a JSON file into apps/web/src/i18n/locales; a switcher appears once there are two.

docker.label: Docker
docker.about: Docker Compose for local services, plus production images for the API and the web app behind nginx. Ship it all with docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up.

ci.label: GitHub Actions + Renovate
ci.about: GitHub Actions run lint, typecheck, tests, the build and Playwright on every push. Renovate keeps dependencies fresh with grouped, scheduled pull requests.

apps-web.label: apps/web
apps-web.about: Components live in apps/web/src/components/ui, right next to the app that uses them. The simplest setup: pnpm ui:add <component> drops new ones there.

packages-ui.label: packages/ui
packages-ui.about: Components, styles and the theme move to a shared @repo/ui workspace, ready for a second app. pnpm ui:add <component> still works: shadcn reads both components.json files and installs into the package.

neutral.label: Neutral
neutral.about: shadcn's default black-and-white look with soft gray accents. Buttons, focus rings and charts stay neutral, so content carries the color.

amber.about: shadcn's Amber theme for buttons, focus rings, the active sidebar item and charts. Change it later by editing --brand in the stylesheet.

recommended.label: Recommended
recommended.about: A solid default: NestJS on Express, email and password sign-in, Postgres in Docker, CI and every API safeguard on. Change anything on the next screens.

saas.label: SaaS starter
saas.hint: OAuth, 2FA, teams, admin, email, uploads, jobs
saas.about: Everything a multi-tenant SaaS needs on day one: OAuth and 2FA, organizations with roles, an admin area, email, uploads and background jobs.

minimal.label: Featherweight
minimal.hint: plain Fastify on SQLite, no Docker
minimal.about: The lightest kit: a plain Fastify API, email and password on SQLite, and nothing to start but pnpm dev. Ideal for prototypes and weekend projects.

everything.label: Kitchen sink
everything.hint: every module, so you can see it all
everything.about: Every module switched on, so you can tour the whole kit and delete what you don't need. Expect Docker for Postgres, Redis and RustFS.
